correctness.rationale: For the exact labelled Kneser graph and single-vertex recolouring definitions, all 1,048,576 four-colour assignments were examined; every legal edge is generated and its reverse verified. All 12,960-source breadth-first searches certify connectivity, radius 13, diameter 14, 3,360/9,600 eccentricity split, 44,400 diametral unordered pairs and the full fourteen-distance vector. A second independently structured recursive-state and S5 x S4 orbit program reconstructs the 11 symmetry orbits, shell profiles, complete pair counts and an explicit 14-step shortest path. Both programs were executed and passed; finite exhaustiveness applies only to P=KG(5,2).

originality.rationale: The exact metric theorem is distinct from classical chromatic counts and from Feghali--Johnson--Paulusma's general Δ+1-colouring component/diameter bounds. Full primary texts inspected for the most relevant same-operation and broader theorems; no diameter 14, radius 13, eleven orbit eccentricity table, or all-pairs distance spectrum appears in the material checked. Targeted exact-parameter, aliases, equivalent-recolouring and broader-theory searches returned no decisive prior implication. Priority remains qualified by potentially unindexed computations, so PASS is best-knowledge rather than a mathematical uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An unindexed, unpublished, differently named or later exact Petersen recolouring enumeration might contain the same metric; lack of an indexed match is not proof of historical priority.
The primary 2007 CDAM report has only month-level dated evidence, so the conservative first-public-date field uses the exact 2010-12-16 online date of its associated article.
This is not an independent human review; two computational implementations can share modelling assumptions, mitigated by explicit Kneser and move definitions and separately structured enumeration.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph, a standard cubic girth-five graph, is the canonical benchmark at the chromatic-plus-one/degree-plus-one recolouring palette. General graph-recolouring theory covers connectivity and polynomial upper bounds but not these sharp distances. The exact radius, diameter, symmetry-stratified eccentricities and full pair-distance spectrum quantify intrinsic optimal transformation costs and furnish an independently reproducible model benchmark. This is a motivated natural complete finite metric classification, not a parameter substitution into a known formula; its value is local and no general-family theorem is claimed.
